questions.prompt: Choose the best heading for this paragraph. (Paragraph 1)
questions.context: Wolves were removed from Yellowstone National Park in the 1920s, and for decades elk grazed freely along the rivers. Young willow and aspen trees were eaten before they could grow. After wolves were reintroduced in 1995, elk changed their behaviour and avoided open valleys. Streamside trees began to recover, and beavers, songbirds and fish are reported to have benefited, although scientists still debate how large the effect has been.
options: The hunting of wolves in the twentieth century
The diet of elk in winter
A predator's return and the disputed effects on a landscape
Tree species of the American West
questions.answer: A predator's return and the disputed effects on a landscape
questions.why: Đoạn nói về việc sói quay lại và tác động còn tranh cãi lên hệ sinh thái. Các lựa chọn khác chỉ là chi tiết.

questions.prompt: Choose the best heading for this paragraph. (Paragraph 2)
questions.context: Lightning strikes the Earth roughly forty times every second. A storm cloud builds up electric charge as ice crystals collide, and when the difference between the cloud and the ground becomes large enough, a channel of super-heated air forms and a current flows. The thunder we hear is the shock wave from that sudden heating, which is why light is seen before sound is heard.
options: The dangers of lightning to humans
How ice crystals form in clouds
The speed of light and sound
The physical causes of lightning and thunder
questions.answer: The physical causes of lightning and thunder
questions.why: Trọng tâm là cơ chế vật lý của sét và sấm. Tốc độ ánh sáng và âm thanh chỉ là phần kết.
questions.quote: a channel of super-heated air forms

questions.prompt: Choose the best heading for this paragraph. (Paragraph 3)
questions.context: Soil is not simply broken rock. A handful of healthy soil contains more living organisms than there are people on Earth, from bacteria and fungi to worms and insects. They break down dead plants, recycle nutrients and bind particles into a crumbly structure that holds water. Farming practices that disturb or poison this community can reduce harvests more than farmers realise.
options: The hidden living community that sustains soil fertility
The use of chemicals in farming
Why worms are useful to gardeners
The number of people on Earth
questions.answer: The hidden living community that sustains soil fertility
questions.why: Ý chính là sinh vật sống tạo nên độ phì nhiêu của đất. Hoá chất nông nghiệp chỉ nhắc cuối đoạn.
questions.quote: more living organisms than there are people

questions.prompt: Choose the best heading for this paragraph. (Paragraph 4)
questions.context: Glaciers act as natural reservoirs. They store winter snow as ice and release meltwater through summer, when rivers downstream are most needed for irrigation and drinking. As temperatures climb, many glaciers are shrinking. At first, rivers may run higher with extra meltwater, but once the ice has largely gone, flows will decline, putting pressure on the hundreds of millions of people who depend on them.
options: How the loss of glaciers threatens future water supplies
The formation of ice in mountain regions
Rising sea levels around the world
questions.answer: How the loss of glaciers threatens future water supplies
questions.why: Trọng tâm là sông băng tan sẽ làm nguồn nước cạn. Tuyết mùa đông và mực nước biển không thuộc ý chính.

questions.prompt: Choose the best heading for this paragraph. (Paragraph 5)
questions.context: Fireflies glow through a chemical reaction in which an enzyme helps a compound called luciferin combine with oxygen, producing light with almost no heat. Each species has its own flash pattern, which males use to attract females of the same species. Some predatory fireflies imitate other species' patterns to lure and eat the males. Artificial lighting at night is now blamed for confusing many populations.
options: The effects of street lighting on towns
The chemistry and signals of firefly light
How males attract females in other species
questions.answer: The chemistry and signals of firefly light
questions.why: Đoạn nói cơ chế phát sáng và tín hiệu của đom đóm. Ánh sáng nhân tạo và loài săn mồi chỉ là chi tiết.

questions.prompt: Choose the best heading for this paragraph. (Paragraph 6)
questions.context: Deserts are not always hot. The Gobi and the Antarctic interior qualify because they receive very little precipitation, whatever their temperature. Many desert animals avoid the heat of day by living underground or becoming active at dusk. Plants have adapted too: some store water in thick stems, others grow roots that spread widely near the surface to catch brief rain.
options: The size of the Gobi Desert
Adaptations that allow life in very dry places
questions.answer: Adaptations that allow life in very dry places
questions.why: Ý chính là cách sinh vật thích nghi với khô hạn. Lựa chọn "luôn nóng" mâu thuẫn bài, còn các lựa chọn khác quá hẹp.

questions.prompt: Choose the best heading for this paragraph. (Paragraph 7)
questions.context: The deep ocean floor was once assumed to be a barren plain. In 1977, however, scientists in a submersible discovered hot springs on the seabed, surrounded by tube worms, clams and crabs. Without sunlight, these communities depend on bacteria that turn chemicals from the vents into food. The discovery showed that life can flourish without the sun and raised hopes of finding it on other worlds.
options: The search for life on other planets
Hot springs as a source of energy
A discovery of life that does not rely on sunlight
questions.answer: A discovery of life that does not rely on sunlight
questions.why: Trọng tâm là sự sống không cần ánh sáng mặt trời. Khám phá hành tinh khác chỉ là hệ quả được nhắc cuối.
questions.quote: life can flourish without the sun

questions.prompt: Choose the best heading for this paragraph. (Paragraph 8)
questions.context: Pollination by insects is worth billions of dollars to farmers each year, yet pollinators are in decline in many regions. Pesticides, loss of wildflower habitats and disease are the main suspects. In some orchards of China, farmers have taken to pollinating by hand, carrying pollen on brushes from tree to tree, a slow and expensive substitute for the work bees once did free of charge.
options: The use of pesticides in orchards
The decline of pollinators and its costs to farming
Hand tools used by fruit growers
questions.answer: The decline of pollinators and its costs to farming
questions.why: Đoạn nói sự suy giảm côn trùng thụ phấn và cái giá cho nông nghiệp. Thụ phấn bằng tay chỉ là ví dụ.

questions.prompt: Choose the best heading for this paragraph. (Paragraph 9)
questions.context: Many rivers have been straightened and enclosed in concrete channels to prevent flooding, but engineers now question the approach. Straight channels speed water downstream and can worsen floods lower down. Several cities have begun restoring natural bends and floodplains, allowing rivers to spill into open land. The projects can cost less than building higher walls and bring wildlife and recreation back to the water.
options: The cost of building flood walls
Restoring natural rivers as a flood-control strategy
questions.answer: Restoring natural rivers as a flood-control strategy
questions.why: Ý chính là phục hồi sông tự nhiên để chống lũ. Xây kênh bê tông là cách cũ bị phê phán.

questions.prompt: Choose the best heading for this paragraph. (Paragraph 10)
questions.context: Seeds travel in surprising ways. Some are carried inside animals that eat the fruit and drop the seeds far away; others cling with tiny hooks to fur and clothing. Maples spin on winged cases, dandelions float on parachutes of hair, and a few plants simply explode, flinging their seeds several metres. Each method helps the offspring avoid competing with the parent plant for light and water.
options: Varied methods by which plants spread their seeds
questions.answer: Varied methods by which plants spread their seeds
questions.why: Đoạn liệt kê nhiều cách phát tán hạt. Mỗi cách chỉ là một ví dụ nên không phải tiêu đề.

questions.prompt: Choose the best heading for this paragraph. (Paragraph 11)
questions.context: The monsoon brings most of South Asia's annual rainfall in a few months. When it arrives on time, farmers sow rice and other crops with confidence; when it is late or weak, harvests fail and food prices climb. Forecasters now combine satellite data with computer models to predict the monsoon's arrival, but its variations from year to year remain difficult to anticipate.
options: The monsoon's importance and the difficulty of forecasting it
The use of satellites in weather forecasting
questions.answer: The monsoon's importance and the difficulty of forecasting it
questions.why: Đoạn vừa nêu tầm quan trọng của gió mùa vừa nêu khó khăn dự báo. Vệ tinh hay lúa chỉ là chi tiết.

questions.prompt: Choose the best heading for this paragraph. (Paragraph 12)
questions.context: Peat bogs cover only three per cent of the planet's land, yet they hold twice as much carbon as all the world's forests combined. Waterlogged conditions prevent dead plants from fully decaying, so carbon builds up over thousands of years. When bogs are drained for farming or fuel, that carbon escapes as carbon dioxide, which is why campaigners urge governments to protect and rewet them.
options: Peatlands as a huge store of carbon worth protecting
The use of peat as fuel
questions.answer: Peatlands as a huge store of carbon worth protecting
questions.why: Trọng tâm là đầm than bùn chứa lượng carbon khổng lồ cần bảo vệ. Các lựa chọn khác chỉ là chi tiết.

questions.prompt: Choose the best heading for this paragraph. (Paragraph 13)
questions.context: Whales sing songs that can last up to twenty minutes and be repeated for hours. Males of each humpback population share a song that changes gradually each season, and populations in the Pacific sometimes adopt new songs from neighbours. Researchers cannot yet say what the songs mean, but evidence suggests that they play a part in courtship or in competing with other males.
options: The unexplained purpose of humpback whale songs
The migration routes of humpback whales
Differences between male and female whales
questions.answer: The unexplained purpose of humpback whale songs
questions.why: Ý chính: bài hát của cá voi vẫn chưa rõ ý nghĩa. "Giao tiếp dưới nước" quá rộng.
questions.quote: cannot yet say what the songs mean

questions.prompt: Choose the best heading for this paragraph. (Paragraph 14)
questions.context: Cities generate heat. Dark roads and roofs absorb sunlight, cars and air conditioners release warm air, and few trees remain to provide shade, so urban centres can be several degrees warmer than surrounding countryside, especially at night. The effect worsens heatwaves and raises energy use. Planners are experimenting with pale paint on roofs, green roofs and more parks to cool neighbourhoods.
options: Why cities are warmer than their surroundings and how to cool them
Differences between day and night temperatures
questions.answer: Why cities are warmer than their surroundings and how to cool them
questions.why: Đoạn nêu nguyên nhân đô thị nóng hơn và biện pháp làm mát. Từng lựa chọn khác chỉ là một phần.

questions.prompt: Choose the best heading for this paragraph. (Paragraph 15)
questions.context: Salt marshes lie where land meets the sea and are flooded by the tide twice a day. Dense grasses slow incoming water and trap sediment, so marshes can build up in height as sea levels rise. They also absorb storm surges and filter pollution before it reaches open water. Many have been drained for farming or building, and conservationists argue that their value has been underestimated.
options: The protective services provided by salt marshes
questions.answer: The protective services provided by salt marshes
questions.why: Đoạn nêu các lợi ích bảo vệ của đầm lầy muối. Thủy triều và nông nghiệp chỉ là chi tiết.
questions.quote: absorb storm surges and filter pollution

questions.prompt: Choose the best heading for this paragraph. (Paragraph 16)
questions.context: Termites build mounds that can rise several metres above the ground, yet the insects themselves are blind and tiny. Inside, a network of tunnels circulates air, keeping the nest at a steady temperature despite fierce heat outside. No individual termite directs the work. Instead, each follows simple rules and responds to the actions of others, and the mound emerges from their combined behaviour.
options: The life cycle of a termite
How simple rules produce complex insect architecture
questions.answer: How simple rules produce complex insect architecture
questions.why: Ý chính: cấu trúc phức tạp xuất phát từ hành vi đơn giản của từng con. Chiều cao tổ chỉ là chi tiết.
questions.quote: No individual termite directs the work

questions.prompt: Choose the best heading for this paragraph. (Paragraph 17)
questions.context: Volcanic eruptions can cool the planet. In 1815 the eruption of Mount Tambora threw so much ash and sulphur into the atmosphere that sunlight was partly blocked, and the following year, 1816, is remembered in Europe and North America as the year without a summer. Crops failed, food prices rose and some historians link the hardship to emigration and unrest.
options: The danger of volcanoes to nearby villages
Famine and emigration in the nineteenth century
A volcanic eruption that altered the climate
questions.answer: A volcanic eruption that altered the climate
questions.why: Trọng tâm là một vụ phun trào làm thay đổi khí hậu. Nạn đói chỉ là hệ quả.

questions.prompt: Choose the best heading for this paragraph. (Paragraph 18)
questions.context: Coastal fog in northern California helps giant redwoods survive long dry summers. The trees absorb moisture directly through their needles and drip it onto the ground, providing as much as a third of their annual water. Scientists worry that warming oceans may reduce fog, which could threaten the oldest stands. Tree-ring records indicate that fog levels have already declined over the last century.
options: Fog as a vital water source for redwood forests
The age of California's oldest trees
Tree rings as records of climate
The timber industry on the west coast
questions.answer: Fog as a vital water source for redwood forests
questions.why: Đoạn nói sương mù cung cấp nước cho rừng thông đỏ. Vòng cây chỉ là bằng chứng phụ.
questions.quote: as much as a third of their annual water

questions.prompt: Choose the best heading for this paragraph. (Paragraph 19)
questions.context: Wildfires have always shaped forests, and some species depend on them. Certain pine cones open only in intense heat, and fire clears undergrowth so that new seedlings receive light. A century of suppressing every fire, however, allowed dead wood to accumulate, making modern fires larger and harder to control. Land managers now carry out controlled burns to reduce fuel and restore a healthier cycle.
options: The species of pine that need fire
Why fire suppression made forest fires worse
questions.answer: Why fire suppression made forest fires worse
questions.why: Ý chính: ngăn mọi đám cháy khiến cháy rừng về sau nặng hơn. Các lựa chọn khác chỉ là chi tiết.

questions.prompt: Choose the best heading for this paragraph. (Paragraph 20)
questions.context: Earthworms were once regarded by farmers as pests, but Charles Darwin spent decades studying them and concluded that they are essential. By dragging leaves underground and eating soil, they mix organic matter into deeper layers, create channels that let water and roots penetrate, and leave castings rich in nutrients. In a single year, a healthy field can have several tonnes of soil per hectare pass through their bodies.
options: The overlooked value of earthworms to the soil
The amount of rainfall on farms
questions.answer: The overlooked value of earthworms to the soil
questions.why: Ý chính là giun đất có ích cho đất, qua nghiên cứu của Darwin. Darwin chỉ là chi tiết bối cảnh.
